Genji and Hanzo Shimada are **brothers**, sons of the leader of the **Shimada clan**, a powerful yakuza-like crime family based in Hanamura, Japan. Hanzo is the elder and was raised as heir. Genji is the younger and was originally a carefree playboy.

**Their father** was the clan's head, commonly identified as **Sojiro Shimada**, though early lore didn't name him. His death set the conflict in motion. The clan elders ordered Hanzo to bring Genji into line with the family's criminal business. When Genji refused, the brothers fought, and Hanzo struck him down, leaving him for dead.

Overwatch recovered Genji, and Dr. Angela Ziegler (Mercy) rebuilt him as a cyborg. He later helped Overwatch/Blackwatch dismantle the Shimada clan and found peace under the omnic monk Zenyatta. Hanzo, consumed by guilt, left the clan and became a wandering mercenary.

The animated short **"Dragons"** depicts their reunion at Shimada Castle, where Genji reveals he survived and urges Hanzo to forgive himself. Since then the brothers have slowly been reconciling, and both are part of the new Overwatch in Overwatch 2.

Winston's ultimate is **Primal Rage**. He transforms into a raging beast and gains:

A **Clash** map has **five capture points** laid out in a line across the map, two on each team's side and one in the center.

The **middle (center) point is activated first.** When a team captures a point, the next objective unlocks one step further toward the losing team's spawn, so the fight moves back and forth along the line. Each capture scores a point, and the first team to reach 5 points wins. Capturing the last point beside the enemy spawn also wins the match outright.

**Horizon Lunar Colony was an Assault (2CP) map, and Blizzard removed Assault from the core game modes in Overwatch 2.**

When Overwatch 2 launched in October 2022, every Assault map left the Quick Play and Competitive rotations. That included Horizon Lunar Colony, Hanamura, Temple of Anubis, Volskaya Industries and Paris. These maps stayed available only in Custom Games and some Arcade modes.

Blizzard's reasons for retiring the mode included:

- **Lopsided, snowbally matches:** Once attackers took the first point, they often rolled straight through the second.
- **Stalemates at chokepoints:** Some points, especially first points, strongly favored defenders. This led to long, frustrating stalls.
- **Poor fit with 5v5:** With one tank instead of two, holding or breaking tight Assault points became even more swingy.

Blizzard replaced the mode with Push in OW2 and later added Clash (Hanaoka, Throne of Anubis) as a spiritual successor to the capture-point idea. Horizon Lunar Colony itself was never reworked into a new mode. That's why it remains limited to Custom Games and Arcade.
